steps.before: 1.1 If $\partial M=\varnothing$, the empty map from $\varnothing\times[0,1)$ is a collar. Otherwise take $X$ on $U$ from [F1]. Write $F(p,t)=\Phi_t(p)$ wherever the local forward solution remains in $U\cap M$. In a boundary chart, extend $X$ smoothly across the face to apply the ordinary local-flow theorem. At $(p,0)$, the differential of $(y,t)\mapsto F(y,t)$ has the $n-1$ face directions and the strictly inward vector $X_p$ as its columns, so it is invertible. The Euclidean inverse function theorem gives a local diffeomorphism of ambient chart neighbourhoods. Since the boundary coordinate of $F(y,t)$ vanishes for $t=0$ and has positive $t$-derivative near $(p,0)$, it has the sign of $t$ there. Thus the restriction to $t\ge0$ is a smooth local collar with image relatively open in $M$. [F1, F2, [[thm-euclidean-inverse-function-theorem]]]

## Remarks

The first two degrees and the augmentations form the following commutative ladder. Here $j_n$ and $q_n$ are the inclusion of the first summand and projection onto the second summand, and $d_n$ denotes the middle differential. The two projective rows are split exact; the bottom row is the original short exact sequence and need not split. The columns continue upwards to the full resolutions.

```tikzcd
0 \arrow[r] & P'_1 \arrow[r, "j_1"] \arrow[d, "d'_1"'] & P'_1\oplus P''_1 \arrow[r, "q_1"] \arrow[d, "d_1"] & P''_1 \arrow[r] \arrow[d, "d''_1"] & 0 \\
0 \arrow[r] & P'_0 \arrow[r, "j_0"] \arrow[d, "\varepsilon'"'] & P'_0\oplus P''_0 \arrow[r, "q_0"] \arrow[d, "\lambda_0"] & P''_0 \arrow[r] \arrow[d, "\varepsilon''"] & 0 \\
0 \arrow[r] & A' \arrow[r, "i"] & A \arrow[r, "p"] & A'' \arrow[r] & 0
```

The augmentation is $\lambda_0=[i\varepsilon',s]$, where $s:P''_0\to A$ is a chosen lift with $ps=\varepsilon''$. Thus $\lambda_0j_0=i\varepsilon'$ and $p\lambda_0=\varepsilon''q_0$. In positive degrees the chain-map identities are $d_nj_n=j_{n-1}d'_n$ and $q_{n-1}d_n=d''_nq_n$; the chosen summand splittings need not be chain maps. In particular, the middle differential need not be block diagonal.

Writing $K_0=\ker\lambda_0$, $K'_0=\ker\varepsilon'$ and $K''_0=\ker\varepsilon''$, and $K_n=\ker d_n$ with the analogous primed notation for $n\geq1$, each stage gives $0\to K'_n\to K_n\to K''_n\to0$. The next epimorphism $P'_{n+1}\oplus P''_{n+1}\twoheadrightarrow K_n$, followed by $K_n\hookrightarrow P'_n\oplus P''_n$, is $d_{n+1}$. Hence consecutive vertical maps compose to zero, including $\lambda_0d_1=0$. This illustrates steps 1.1 and 2.1; the proof is independent of the diagram.

## Remarks

In this low-degree part of the first-quadrant grid, the original horizontal
index increases to the right and the original vertical index increases upward.
Every square anticommutes: $hv=-vh$; the squares are not asserted to commute.

```tikzcd
C_{0,2} \arrow[d,"v"'] & C_{1,2} \arrow[l,"h"'] \arrow[d,"v"'] & C_{2,2} \arrow[l,"h"'] \arrow[d,"v"] \\
C_{0,1} \arrow[d,"v"'] & C_{1,1} \arrow[l,"h"'] \arrow[d,"v"'] & C_{2,1} \arrow[l,"h"'] \arrow[d,"v"] \\
C_{0,0} & C_{1,0} \arrow[l,"h"'] & C_{2,0} \arrow[l,"h"']
```

The grid continues upward and to the right; components with a negative index
are zero. The cutoff $F^{\mathrm{row}}_1T$ retains rows $0$ and $1$, and its
quotient by $F^{\mathrm{row}}_0T$ retains only row $1$. More generally the
row-$p$ quotient has $E^0_{p,q}=C_{q,p}$ and differential $h$. Taking horizontal
homology turns the downward arrows into the following part of the page-one chain, for
any fixed $q\ge0$:

```tikzcd
E^1_{2,q}=H^h_q(C_{*,2}) \arrow[d,"d^1=v_*"] \\
E^1_{1,q}=H^h_q(C_{*,1}) \arrow[d,"d^1=v_*"] \\
E^1_{0,q}=H^h_q(C_{*,0})
```

Here $v_*[x]=[vx]$, with no additional sign because the total differential
is $h+v$. Thus $d^1$ has bidegree $(-1,0)$ in spectral coordinates, and the
chain continues upward, and its homology at index $p$ is $E^2_{p,q}=H^v_p(H^h_q(C))$.
These diagrams illustrate the filtration and page calculation; the proof above
is independent of them.
